mechanism: JNJ-81201887 is an investigational recombinant adeno-associated viral vector gene therapy, described by J&J as AAVCAGsCD59/JNJ-1887, that expresses soluble CD59 in retinal cells. Soluble CD59 is intended to inhibit formation of the complement membrane attack complex, the terminal step of complement-mediated cell lysis, after a single intravitreal injection.
phase: Phase 2 long-term extension; completed Phase 2b parent study; J&J's April 2026 development pipeline lists JNJ-1887 sCD59 for geographic atrophy in Phase 2.
development_status: ClinicalTrials.gov lists NCT06635148 as a recruiting Phase 2 long-term extension of JNJ-81201887 parent studies in participants with geographic atrophy secondary to AMD. The extension started on 2024-09-19, estimates enrollment of 274, has estimated primary completion on 2029-08-24 and estimated study completion on 2030-07-16, and gives no study intervention in the LTE. The randomized Phase 2b parent study NCT05811351 completed on 2026-02-23 with actual enrollment of 305, but no ClinicalTrials.gov results are posted. J&J's current pipeline still places JNJ-1887 sCD59 in Phase 2, with no disclosed filing or launch timing.
expected_launch_window: 2031 or later unless Janssen advances using the completed Phase 2b dataset on an accelerated or otherwise shortened regulatory path
clinical_summary: The clinical rationale is differentiated because JNJ-81201887 is designed as a one-time intravitreal AAV therapy targeting terminal complement activity through soluble CD59, while approved GA complement therapies require repeated intravitreal dosing. The Phase 2b parent study used change in square-root GA lesion area at Month 18 and U.S.-specific rate of change in untransformed GA lesion area as primary endpoints, with visual function and patient-reported outcomes as secondary endpoints. Phase 1 GA data in 17 patients showed a manageable safety profile and no dose-limiting adverse events, but the small open-label study found GA lesion growth was similar across dose cohorts overall and the randomized Phase 2b results are not yet public. Differentiation remains meaningful but not high until controlled efficacy, durability, inflammation management, and wet-AMD conversion data are available.
safety_summary: NCT06635148 is focused on long-term ocular and systemic TEAEs, clinical laboratory abnormalities, and retinal imaging or eye-exam abnormalities for up to 5 years after parent-study dosing. In the Phase 1 GA study, J&J reported no dose-limiting toxicities, no serious/systemic/fatal AEs related to treatment, and 6 mild ocular inflammation events in 5 of 17 patients; most resolved with topical steroids or observation, with one unresolved vitritis event managed by observation in a patient who later had an unrelated fatal leukemia AE. The Phase 2b parent protocol used oral prednisone and periocular triamcinolone prophylaxis, signaling inflammation management as a key launch consideration. Approved GA analog labels and policies highlight monitoring for endophthalmitis, retinal detachment, retinal vasculitis/vascular occlusion, intraocular inflammation, increased intraocular pressure, and neovascular AMD.
management_tools: Track Phase 2b NCT05811351 results, conference abstracts, registry results posting, and any Janssen Phase 3 or BLA guidance before building final controls.
Medical-benefit prior authorization for any future launch, requiring labeled diagnosis of GA secondary to AMD and retinal specialist prescribing/administration.

Require baseline fundus autofluorescence or OCT documentation of GA lesion area, study-eye/labeled-eye laterality, foveal involvement status, visual acuity, and absence of active ocular infection or active intraocular inflammation.
Use quantity controls tied to the final label, likely one intravitreal JNJ-81201887 administration per treated eye unless retreatment is supported.
Require documentation of corticosteroid prophylaxis and inflammation-monitoring plan if included in the final label or REMS-like risk controls.

Continuation/outcomes monitoring should capture GA lesion growth, BCVA/low-luminance visual acuity, conversion to neovascular AMD, ocular inflammation, IOP changes, retinal vasculitis/occlusion, and need for anti-VEGF therapy.
Avoid duplicate payment for overlapping chronic GA complement therapy in the same eye unless combination or sequential therapy is specifically supported by the label and evidence.
Plan medical-benefit contracting scenarios for one-time therapy, including outcomes-based agreements, installment payment, stop-loss/reinsurance exposure, and site-of-care requirements.
evidence_gaps: No ClinicalTrials.gov results are posted for NCT06635148 or the completed randomized Phase 2b parent study NCT05811351.
No public Phase 2b topline efficacy or safety press release was found for JNJ-81201887 in GA.
No Phase 3, registration, BLA submission, FDA designation, PDUFA date, or U.S. launch timing was found.
Parent study 81201887MDG1003 is named in the LTE record, but a directly linked public NCT record was not found.
Final launch dose, whether one or both eyes may be treated, retreatment rules, steroid prophylaxis requirements, and long-term inflammation risk remain unknown.
No public JNJ-81201887 price exists; annual cost range is analog-derived and may understate or overstate final one-time gene therapy pricing.

sources.title: Long-term Extension Study for Participants With Geographic Atrophy (GA) Secondary to Age-related Macular Degeneration (AMD) in JNJ-81201887 Parent Clinical Studies
supports: Assigned trial record for JNJ-81201887 in GA secondary to AMD.
Sponsor is Janssen Research & Development, LLC; other identifiers include 81201887MDG3002 and EUCT 2022-500747-21-00.
Overall status is recruiting; phase is Phase 2; actual start was 2024-09-19; estimated primary completion is 2029-08-24; estimated completion is 2030-07-16; estimated enrollment is 274.
Study is a long-term safety extension of a single intravitreal dose administered in parent studies 81201887MDG2001/NCT05811351 and 81201887MDG1003.
No study intervention will be administered in the LTE; arms reflect prior low-dose JNJ-81201887, high-dose JNJ-81201887, and sham parent-study assignments.
Primary outcomes are ocular and systemic TEAEs, abnormal clinical laboratory assessments, and abnormal retinal imaging or eye-exam findings for up to 5 years.
ClinicalTrials.gov hasResults is false.

sources.title: A Study to Evaluate Intravitreal JNJ-81201887 (AAVCAGsCD59) Compared to Sham Procedure for the Treatment of Geographic Atrophy (GA) Secondary to Age-related Macular Degeneration (AMD)
supports: Phase 2b randomized, double-masked, multicenter, dose-ranging, sham-controlled parent study of intravitreal JNJ-81201887/AAVCAGsCD59 in GA secondary to AMD.
Overall status is completed; actual start was 2023-03-06; actual primary completion and study completion were 2026-02-23; actual enrollment was 305.
Interventions included single low-dose or high-dose intravitreal JNJ-81201887, oral prednisone, periocular triamcinolone, and sham/placebo comparators.
Primary endpoints were global change from baseline in square-root GA lesion area at Month 18 and U.S.-specific rate of change in untransformed GA lesion area from baseline to Month 18.
Secondary outcomes included LLVA, reading speed, microperimetry, BCVA, FRI Index, and NEI-VFQ-25 composite score at Month 18.
ClinicalTrials.gov hasResults is false.

sources.title: Treatment of Advanced Dry Age Related Macular Degeneration With AAVCAGsCD59
supports: Completed Phase 1 open-label dose-escalation study of a single intravitreal injection of AAVCAGsCD59/HMR59 in advanced dry AMD with GA.
Actual enrollment was 17; actual primary completion was 2017-12-06 and actual study completion was 2019-12-09.
Registry description states AAVCAGsCD59 increases soluble CD59 expression to inhibit membrane attack complex formation, the terminal step of complement-mediated cell lysis.
Primary outcome was ocular and systemic adverse events through 26 weeks; secondary outcomes included GA area, GA growth rate, conversion to wet AMD, drusen volume, and 15-letter visual acuity loss.
ClinicalTrials.gov hasResults is false.

sources.title: JNJ-81201887 Medical Information: Phase 1 Clinical Trials
supports: J&J describes JNJ-1887/JNJ-81201887/AAVCAGsCD59 as an investigational recombinant AAV gene therapy being studied for GA and wet AMD.
Mechanism is AAV serotype 2 expression of soluble CD59 intended to inhibit membrane attack complex formation and protect retinal cells after a single in-office intravitreal injection.
Study 1001 was a 24-month open-label Phase 1 GA study with 17 patients.
Phase 1 GA dosing cohorts were 3.56 x 10^10 vg, 1.071 x 10^11 vg, and 3.56 x 10^11 vg without corticosteroid prophylaxis.
J&J reported no dose-limiting AEs, no serious/systemic/fatal AEs related to JNJ-1887, and no related AEs leading to discontinuation in Study 1001.

J&J reported 6 mild ocular inflammation events in 5 of 17 patients, with inflammation findings resolved at last assessment; no retinal vasculitis, endophthalmitis, or new-onset CNV occurred in treated eyes.

sources.title: Phase 1 Study of JNJ-81201887 Gene Therapy in Geographic Atrophy Secondary to Age-Related Macular Degeneration
supports: Published Phase 1 study evaluated safety and tolerability of single intravitreal JNJ-81201887/JNJ-1887 in GA secondary to advanced dry AMD.
Seventeen patients were enrolled into low, intermediate, and high dose cohorts and followed over 24 months.
Authors reported JNJ-81201887 was well tolerated, with no dose-limiting AEs and no serious or systemic AEs related to study intervention.
Five of 17 patients experienced mild treatment-related ocular inflammation; no endophthalmitis or new-onset choroidal neovascularization was reported.
GA lesion growth rate was similar among cohorts overall; in the high-dose cohort, mean square-root lesion growth declined from months 0-6 to months 18-24.
Authors concluded further investigation for GA treatment was warranted.

sources.title: Johnson & Johnson Selected Innovative Medicines in Development as of April 14, 2026
supports: J&J pipeline lists JNJ-1887 sCD59 for geographic atrophy within the neuroscience pipeline.
Pipeline page context shows Phase 1, Phase 2, Phase 3, and registration categories; JNJ-1887 sCD59 is listed in the Phase 2 section for GA.
Footnote states JNJ-1887 is associated with Hemera Biosciences under strategic partnerships, collaborations, and licensing arrangements.

sources.title: Johnson & Johnson Innovative Medicine: Ophthalmology
supports: J&J describes geographic atrophy as an advanced form of AMD that is progressive and irreversible and leads to permanent central vision loss.
J&J states GA is the leading cause of blindness in people over age 65 and estimates about 8 million people are living with the disease.
J&J states there is currently no cure for GA.
J&J describes its ophthalmology approach as developing breakthrough therapies to preserve and restore sight in blinding retinal conditions.

sources.title: DailyMed: SYFOVRE (pegcetacoplan injection), for intravitreal use
supports: Syfovre is a complement inhibitor indicated for treatment of GA secondary to AMD.
Recommended dose is 15 mg by intravitreal injection to each affected eye once every 25 to 60 days.
Warnings include endophthalmitis and retinal detachments, retinal vasculitis and/or retinal vascular occlusion, neovascular AMD, intraocular inflammation, and increased intraocular pressure.
Common adverse reactions include ocular discomfort, neovascular AMD, vitreous floaters, and conjunctival hemorrhage.

sources.title: DailyMed: IZERVAY (avacincaptad pegol injection)
supports: Izervay is a complement inhibitor indicated for treatment of GA secondary to AMD.
Recommended dose is 2 mg by intravitreal injection to each affected eye once monthly, approximately every 28 days.
Warnings and precautions include endophthalmitis and retinal detachments, neovascular AMD, and increased intraocular pressure.
Common adverse reactions include conjunctival hemorrhage, increased intraocular pressure, blurred vision, and neovascular AMD.

sources.title: Oklahoma Health Care Authority Drug Utilization Review Board Packet, June 12, 2024
supports: Cost comparison for complement inhibitors lists Izervay 2 mg/0.1 mL at $2,100 per dose and $27,300 per year for one eye at every-4-week dosing.
Cost comparison lists Syfovre 15 mg/0.1 mL at $2,190 per dose and $28,470 per year for one eye at every-4-week dosing.
Costs do not reflect rebated prices or net costs and are based on NADAC, WAC, or SMAC.

Recommended Izervay approval criteria included FDA-approved GA secondary to dry AMD, absence of ocular/periocular infection or active intraocular inflammation, ophthalmologist or experienced intravitreal-injection prescriber/administrator, monitoring for endophthalmitis, retinal detachment, IOP increase, and neovascular AMD, and quantity limit of one vial per eye once monthly for up to 12 months.

sources.title: Cigna: LUXTURNA - First gene therapy to treat a rare form of inherited vision loss
supports: Luxturna is an FDA-approved ocular gene therapy manufactured by Spark Therapeutics.
Cigna reported Luxturna WAC of $425,000 per eye or $850,000 for both eyes.
Luxturna is covered under medical benefit plans subject to medical necessity review.
Cigna described one course of therapy as one injection per eye and noted potential outcomes-based contracts, direct contracting, and installment payment approaches.

sources.title: Aetna Clinical Policy Bulletin 1029: Pegcetacoplan Intravitreal Injection (Syfovre)
supports: Aetna requires precertification for Syfovre in applicable commercial medical plans.
Criteria require diagnosis of GA secondary to AMD and prescribing by or in consultation with an ophthalmologist.
Continuation requires positive clinical response such as reduction or stabilization in vision decline risk or stabilization/reduction in total GA lesion area.
Aetna excludes GA secondary to non-AMD etiologies such as Stargardt disease, cone-rod dystrophy, and toxic maculopathies.

sources.title: Aetna Clinical Policy Bulletin 1041: Avacincaptad Pegol (Izervay)
supports: Aetna requires precertification for Izervay in applicable plans.
Aetna commercial brand-selection language considers Izervay medically necessary only after contraindication, intolerance, or ineffective response to lower-cost Syfovre for GA secondary to AMD.
Criteria require GA secondary to AMD and prescribing by or in consultation with an ophthalmologist.
Continuation requires positive clinical response such as maintenance in BCVA or visual field or reduction in vision decline or severe vision-loss risk.
Policy describes Izervay as a C5 inhibitor that may decrease membrane attack complex formation.

expected_launch_window.value: 2031 or later unless Janssen advances using the completed Phase 2b dataset on an accelerated or otherwise shortened regulatory path
expected_launch_window.method: Used current Phase 2 pipeline status, completed but unpublished Phase 2b parent study, ongoing LTE estimated to complete in 2030, and absence of public Phase 3, filing, or launch guidance.
expected_launch_window.explanation: A near-term launch is not source-supported. The program could move faster if the completed Phase 2b study is treated as registrational or triggers an expedited path, but public sources currently support monitoring as a Phase 2 asset with long-term safety follow-up extending to 2030.

annual_cost_range.method: Used current GA complement therapy as the low analog at $27,300 per year for one eye at every-4-week Izervay dosing and one-time ocular gene therapy Luxturna WAC of $425,000 per eye as the high analog for a first-year treated-eye cost.
annual_cost_range.explanation: No JNJ-81201887 price exists. The low end reflects the annual one-eye cost of an approved intravitreal GA complement inhibitor; the high end reflects a one-time ocular gene therapy WAC per eye. The range excludes rebates, medical administration, imaging, corticosteroid prophylaxis, anti-VEGF rescue, bilateral treatment, facility fees, and outcomes-based contracting.

clinical_differentiation.method: Balanced potentially durable one-time intravitreal AAV-mediated terminal complement inhibition against approved repeated-dose intravitreal complement inhibitors, while discounting for missing randomized Phase 2b results.
clinical_differentiation.explanation: The route and durability concept could materially change GA management if efficacy and long-term safety are confirmed. The current rating stops short of high because Phase 1 was small and open-label, Phase 2b results are not public, and inflammation/wet-AMD monitoring could affect uptake.

budget_impact.method: Assessed analog drug costs, medical-benefit administration, possible one-time gene therapy pricing, large older-adult GA population, bilateral-disease potential, and existing payer controls for GA complement inhibitors.
budget_impact.explanation: Even with slower launch timing, a one-time AAV therapy for a prevalent Medicare-heavy ophthalmology indication could create high first-year medical-benefit exposure if priced closer to gene therapy analogs.

disruption_risk.method: Rated from Phase 2 status, completed unpublished Phase 2b parent study, long LTE through 2030, lack of filing guidance, and potentially disruptive one-time administration if efficacy is positive.
disruption_risk.explanation: Operational disruption is not imminent, but the asset could alter current repeated-injection GA pathways and medical-benefit contracting if controlled data support durable benefit.

recommended_action.method: Matched action to current Phase 2 status, no posted Phase 2b results, no disclosed filing timeline, and high but uncertain future budget impact.
recommended_action.explanation: Monitor for Phase 2b readout and regulatory-path clarity before drafting final coverage policy; maintain early scenario notes for one-time ophthalmic gene therapy pricing and outcomes-based contracting.

quality_flags: Assigned NCT06635148 is an LTE with no study intervention administered; efficacy interpretation requires the parent Phase 2b study NCT05811351 and any undisclosed/nonpublic 81201887MDG1003 data.
NCT05811351 is completed but has no posted ClinicalTrials.gov results as of this review.
J&J pipeline still lists JNJ-1887 sCD59 for GA as Phase 2 as of 2026-04-14; no Phase 3 or registration source was found.
Annual cost is analog-derived because no JNJ-81201887 price exists; low end uses current GA complement-inhibitor annual treated-eye cost and high end uses Luxturna ocular gene therapy WAC per eye.
The cost range is per first treated eye for planning; bilateral treatment, administration, imaging, steroid prophylaxis, monitoring, and rescue anti-VEGF costs could materially change budget impact.

Clinical differentiation depends on unpublished controlled Phase 2b efficacy and long-term safety, especially ocular inflammation, retinal vasculitis/vascular occlusion, increased IOP, and neovascular AMD conversion.
